name: Adyen
summary: A global payment platform and acquirer for larger businesses needing online, in-person, marketplace, and multi-region payment infrastructure.

pricing.headline: A fixed processing fee plus a payment-method fee; card economics can use interchange-plus-plus pricing.
pricing.assumptions: No single universal checkout rate. Obtain country, method, volume, and acquiring terms.

sellerCoverage: Adyen onboards eligible businesses in supported regions through a sales and underwriting process.
buyerCoverage: Global acquiring and payment-method coverage varies by merchant entity, market, and integration.
products: Eligible enterprise commerce, platforms, marketplaces, online and in-person businesses.

features.checkout: Web, mobile, hosted components, API, and point-of-sale integrations.
features.subscriptions: Tokenization and recurring-payment support rather than an opinionated SaaS billing catalog. Billing and loyalty capabilities expanded via the closed Talon.One and Orb acquisitions (2026-07-01); no public rate change.
features.invoicing: Payment infrastructure can support invoice collection; billing and quoting may require another layer.
features.paymentMethods: A broad global directory of cards, wallets, bank methods, BNPL, and local methods.
features.payouts: Settlement schedules and currencies are defined in merchant terms.

responsibilities.note: The business remains merchant and seller.
Payment acquiring does not transfer product-sale tax responsibility.
Adyen provides risk and dispute tools while the merchant owns policies and exposure.
The merchant builds or integrates these operating layers.

limitations: Often requires separate SaaS billing and tax operations
avoidIf: You are an early creator seeking instant setup
